idiom_name: recording double that logs calls for after-the-fact assertions
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: install a double that exposes the collaborator's interface, delegates to the real implementation when behaviour must be preserved, and appends every invocation (method, arguments, order, thrown error) to a per-test log. After the SUT has run, assert against the log - call counts, argument values, relative order - rather than declaring expectations before the run. The log is test state: reset or recreate it between tests and keep it out of production paths; where the language cannot intercept calls, the seam is a constructor parameter, interface or function pointer.
code_sketch:
spy = RecordingDouble(real_collaborator)   # same interface, delegates by default
sut = SystemUnderTest(spy)

sut.run()                                    # real code path executes

assert spy.call_count("send") == 1           # assert after the fact
assert spy.calls("send")[0].args == ("bob@example.com", body)
pitfalls: Asserting on every recorded call turns the test into a transcription of the implementation; assert only the interactions the contract requires.
A spy that wraps the real collaborator still performs its side effects (mail, network, disk) unless the wrapped implementation is itself replaced.
The call log is mutable shared state; concurrent SUT code needs a synchronised or per-thread log, or the assertions race.

Wrong move: stubbing a method on a spy and still asserting that the real implementation ran -> the stub already replaced that behaviour, so the delegation assertion passes vacuously or the real side effect double-executes -> instead keep record-only spies and stub-where-needed doubles separate, and assert delegation only on the methods left unstubbed.

Wrong move: adding verifyNoMoreInteractions/no-more-calls to every spy test -> each innocuous new call (a log line, a metrics bump) fails unrelated tests, turning the spy into an over-specified mock (Mockito's own javadoc warns it makes tests brittle) -> instead verify the handful of interactions the contract names and use never() only for calls that are specifically forbidden.

Wrong move: reading the call log right after kicking off async SUT work -> the recording races the assertion and the test fails intermittently -> instead await the SUT's completion (promise, future, join) before inspecting the log, and keep one log per test.
